title: ZeroDeck Cross-Cutting System Requirements
scope: Cross-capability system and operational product requirements applying across ZeroDeck web and Android; excludes capability-specific implementation details and technology/architecture selection.

statements.text: The system MUST resolve the same ZeroDeck account principal across supported web and Android sessions when the user signs into the same account.
The system MUST communicate material differences in capability, permission, availability, or data access between web and Android before the user relies on an affected operation.
The system MUST enforce protected account, entitlement, owner-activation, and administrative authorization decisions at a trusted service boundary rather than relying solely on client-supplied state.
The system MUST preserve active Pro entitlement and owner-controlled activation as independent prerequisites for every MVP-03 provider/API call.

The system MUST deny newly evaluated protected operations and MUST prevent queued or not-yet-dispatched provider work after the authoritative service records revocation of the relevant access, entitlement, permission, or owner activation. Already-dispatched work MUST be cancelled where supported and MUST NOT initiate subsequent provider calls.
The system MUST associate each category of personal, file-derived, URL-derived, account, and operational data it processes with a documented product purpose and authorized access boundary.
The system MUST disclose data to an external service only to the extent required for the user-requested operation and permitted by the applicable product contract and user notice.
The system MUST provide a documented lifecycle policy for each category of system-managed user data, including purpose, retention trigger, deletion behaviour, and exceptions.

The system MUST prevent private credentials, signing material, provider secrets, and other server-only secrets from exposure through public client configuration, user-facing responses, or ordinary diagnostics.
The system MUST validate required operational configuration before enabling the affected capability and fail closed when that configuration is missing, malformed, or inconsistent.
The system MUST keep development, test, and production credentials, data, and operational controls distinguishable and prevent non-production values from authorizing production operations.
The system MUST NOT report a dependent operation as successful when a required service or dependency has failed, timed out, or returned unusable data.
The system MUST limit the user-visible impact of a failed optional or independent dependency to capabilities that require that dependency.
The system MUST define which backend-managed records are recoverable from service or storage failure and identify consequences when recovery is not possible.
The system MUST verify integrity and authorization context of restored backend-managed state before using it to authorize protected operations.
The system MUST retain an appropriately access-controlled record of administrative changes affecting account access, entitlement, owner activation, or protected capability availability.
The system MUST exclude raw credentials, secret values, unnecessary file contents, and unredacted sensitive URL components from ordinary application diagnostics.

The system MUST expose sufficient operational health information for an authorized operator to distinguish service unavailability, dependency failure, and capability-specific degradation without exposing user content or secrets.
The system MUST support recording the scope, timeline, affected capabilities, containment action, and resolution status of a material security or availability incident.
The system MUST enforce documented bounds for resource-consuming operations and storage categories before enabling them for general use.
statements.location: ### Requirement ZD-SYS-020 — Bounded shared resource use

statements.text: The system MUST respond to resource exhaustion or overload with an explicit bounded rejection, deferral, or degraded state rather than silently accepting work it cannot safely complete.
The system MUST identify each production-critical external dependency, its purpose, owner, failure impact, and replacement or exit consideration before production reliance.
The system MUST treat data returned by an external dependency as untrusted input and validate it before using it to affect account state, security outcomes, or subsequent operations.
The system MUST define duplicate-request behaviour for each cross-platform state-changing operation so retries do not create unintended duplicate effects.
The system MUST make provenance and intended release identity of production software artifacts verifiable before accepting them as product updates.
The system MUST identify and handle unsupported or incompatible client/service version combinations before executing operations with unsupported semantics or security assumptions.
The system MUST communicate whether a requested capability is available, unavailable, degraded, incomplete, or completed without implying another capability was also performed.
The system MUST identify which system-managed account data can be exported or made available to the account holder and which categories are excluded with a documented reason.
statements.location: ### Requirement ZD-SYS-028 — Data portability and account closure

requirements.subject: Shared account identity
preconditions: Same account is used on both platforms
inputs: User signs in on each platform
outcomes: Both sessions resolve to the same account principal; session credentials remain independently controlled.
forbiddenBehaviors: The system MUST NOT create unrelated account principals for the same ZeroDeck account solely because the user is on a different supported platform.
requirements.rationale: Owner direction: one product identity across web and Android; detailed session policy remains in authentication contract.

basis.description: Owner direction: one product identity across web and Android; detailed session policy remains in authentication contract.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Same account is used on both platforms
acceptanceCriteria.when: User signs in on each platform
acceptanceCriteria.then: Both sessions resolve to the same account principal; session credentials remain independently controlled.

assumptions: Product-level outcome; implementation mechanism remains undecided.
constraints: No architecture, vendor, numeric service target, or legal policy is selected by this requirement.

openQuestions.question: What availability objective, if any, is required for the MVP and each capability?
openQuestions.impact: Cannot define service acceptance or commitments without an agreed target.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Set internal availability targets before launch, but do not publish uptime commitments until reliability and operating-cost evidence supports them.

openQuestions.question: What recovery time and recovery point objectives apply to backend-managed account, entitlement, activation and audit state?
openQuestions.impact: Determines backup frequency, recovery design and user impact.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Define RTO/RPO for backend-managed account, entitlement, activation and audit state after data criticality and recovery analysis. No numeric values are selected in product design.

openQuestions.question: Which backend-managed data categories require backup, and which must never be backed up?
openQuestions.impact: Prevents assuming user file bytes or quarantine contents belong in backend backups.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Back up only necessary backend-managed data. User file bytes and quarantine content/keys are not included in backend backups by default.

openQuestions.question: What retention and expiry rules apply to backups, audit events, diagnostics and incident records?
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Maintain separate retention/expiry policies for backups, audit events, diagnostics and incident records. Exact durations and statutory exceptions require legal and architecture review.

openQuestions.question: What data classification scheme and access roles govern account, file-derived, URL-derived and operational data?
openQuestions.impact: Determines access boundaries and handling obligations.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Classify account, file-derived, URL-derived and operational data by sensitivity and define least-privilege access. Exact classification taxonomy and role mapping belong to architecture/security design.

openQuestions.question: Which jurisdictions and legal/privacy obligations apply at launch?
openQuestions.impact: Legal basis, notice, retention and notification depend on geography and service model.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Confirm launch jurisdictions and applicable privacy/legal obligations with qualified review before release. No jurisdiction-specific legal conclusion is made in Phase 9.

openQuestions.question: Which operational events may be logged, at what detail, and who may access them?
openQuestions.impact: Balances debugging/audit needs against privacy and abuse risk.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Log only necessary operational/security events. Exclude passwords, secrets, file contents and sensitive URL components from ordinary diagnostics. Exact event fields and access permissions belong to architecture.

openQuestions.question: What incident severity levels, escalation owners and notification rules are required?
openQuestions.impact: Cannot define response timing or notification commitments.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Define incident severity, accountable escalation owners and user/regulatory notification rules before production. Exact roles, response times and statutory duties require operations/legal review.

openQuestions.question: What numeric limits apply to concurrency, request rates, storage, timeouts and resource consumption?
openQuestions.impact: Bounded behaviour is required, but values are not invented.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Set concurrency, request, storage, timeout and resource limits from workload, platform, safety and cost testing. No arbitrary numeric defaults are approved.

openQuestions.question: What supported browser, Android OS/device and backend compatibility windows apply?
openQuestions.impact: Determines safe compatibility and end-of-support behaviour.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Publish a tested compatibility matrix and end-of-support policy. Exact browser, Android OS/device and backend version windows require testing and owner scope confirmation.

openQuestions.question: What release/update channels, provenance trust roots, rollback policy and emergency withdrawal process are approved?
openQuestions.impact: Concrete trust and recovery policy remains unresolved.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Production updates must have verifiable provenance, signed release artifacts, rollback capability and emergency withdrawal procedures. Trust roots, release channels and operational mechanisms are architecture decisions.

openQuestions.question: Which external dependencies are approved for production, and who owns provider review/exit decisions?
openQuestions.impact: Production reliance, commercial exposure and data processing cannot be assumed.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Approve external dependencies individually only after purpose, terms, privacy/security, cost, failure impact and exit options are reviewed; each production-critical dependency must have a named accountable owner. Specific vendors remain unselected.

openQuestions.question: What authorization/entitlement/activation propagation bound applies across web, Android and in-flight operations?
openQuestions.impact: Explicitly unresolved in authentication and MVP-03 contracts.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Use the shared gate-revocation invariant in ZD-Q-AUTH-013 and ZD-Q-WEB-011/012. Newly evaluated and queued/not-yet-dispatched protected work is denied after revocation; already-dispatched work is cancelled where supported. Exact propagation bounds require architecture testing.

openQuestions.question: What account-data export categories and formats, if any, are in launch scope?
openQuestions.impact: No unapproved export feature is added.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: A dedicated account-data export feature is out of MVP unless a confirmed legal requirement makes it necessary. This does not remove any applicable legal access right.

openQuestions.question: How should conflicting cross-platform updates to shared account state be resolved?
openQuestions.impact: Avoids inconsistent account, subscription or settings state.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Server-authoritative account, entitlement and activation state prevails over stale client state. Conflict/version resolution and synchronization mechanics are architecture decisions.

openQuestions.question: What maintenance windows and user-notice expectations apply?
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Give users advance notice of planned maintenance where practical. Exact windows, channels and notice periods are deferred to operations planning.

openQuestions.question: How does account deletion propagate into backups and immutable audit records?
openQuestions.impact: Must reconcile deletion, justified retention and recoverability.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Account deletion must propagate through backup lifecycle. Immutable audit data may be retained only where justified, minimized and documented with reason and retention period. Exact expiry and legal exceptions require legal/architecture review.

openQuestions.question: What service ownership and support response expectations apply after launch?
openQuestions.impact: Determines operational accountability and support promises.
openQuestions.pmRecommendation: Keep unresolved until the Product Owner records a decision supported by applicable evidence.
openQuestions.resolution: Do not promise a support SLA until a real support channel, accountable owner and operating capacity exist. Define the channel and realistic response expectations before production commitments.
